title: Low-field Imaging For Encephalopathy after Cardiac Arrest
summary:
Background:
Thanks to rapid resuscitation measures, many people survive sudden cardiac arrest. However, a lack of oxygen to the brain during the event often leads to brain injury. Shortly after resuscitation, it is difficult to determine how severe this injury is and what the long-term consequences will be. An early and reliable prognosis is important to guide further treatment and to inform patients and their families. Existing diagnostic methods are complex and not always available. A new mobile brain imaging technique may provide additional helpful information in this situation.

Research question:
The aim of this study is to investigate whether a mobile brain imaging method (ultra-low-field-MRI)  that can be used directly at the patient’s bedside can detect brain injury after cardiac arrest at an early stage and improve the prediction of long-term neurological outcome compared to current standard assessments alone.

Methods:
This observational study includes adult patients who have been successfully resuscitated after a non-traumatic cardiac arrest and are treated in an intensive care unit. In addition to standard clinical examinations, participants will receive an additional mobile brain imaging examination directly at the bedside within a few days after the event. This examination is painless and non-invasive. The images obtained will be analyzed later and compared with results from standard examinations. The neurological status, daily functioning and quality of life of the participants will be assessed by telephone interviews one month and six months after the cardiac arrest. The study aims to determine whether this new method can provide additional value in assessing long-term outcomes after cardiac arrest.
conditions: Anoxic brain damage, not elsewhere classified

interventions.name: Adult patients after non‑traumatic cardiac arrest with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) who are admitted to the intensive care unit.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Non-traumatic cardiac arrest with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC)
Exclusion criteria:
Additional acute cerebral events on the initial brain computed tomography scan (e.g. clearly demarcated territorial ischemic stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, or severe traumatic brain injury).

Patients with implanted devices that are not fully compatible with ultra‑low‑field magnetic resonance imaging (e.g. non‑magnetic‑resonance‑compatible pacemakers, left ventricular assist devices, or Impella systems).
